Definition: morally wrong; concretely, an (actively) bad person
BiblicalUsage: Rasha' is the wicked — morally wrong, and concretely, the actively bad person. The psalm begins, 'Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly'; it says the ungodly 'are like the chaff which the wind driveth away'; the Proverb says, 'The LORD will not suffer the soul of the righteous to famish: but he casteth away the substance of the wicked'; and Ezekiel says, 'But if the wicked will turn from all his sins that he hath committed, and keep all my statutes, and do that which is lawful and right, he shall surely live, he shall not die.'
TheologicalSignificance: The lesson I take is that 'wicked' is the Bible's plainest word for the one who does wrong on purpose: not the weak, not the mistaken, but the one who chooses evil and keeps choosing it. And my position is that Ezekiel's promise is the whole gospel in one verse — if the wicked will turn, he shall surely live, he shall not die — because God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked.
